title: Measuring Meta-Cultural Competency: A Spectral Framework for LLM Knowledge Structures
claim: Evaluation should combine fine-grained factual tests with structural analysis of knowledge, validated end-to-end through a downstream user-facing simulation.
layout: Nested colored regions, left-to-right flows, three linked modules converging on central awareness outputs
description: A dense, color-coded system diagram with three regions. The top-left tan region, Macrostructure Analysis, shows users feeding four scatter plots of real-world knowledge structures (HH, HL, LH, LL). Below is a per-domain pipeline: for each country, a prompt goes to a model, which outputs logprobs. These become a country-country adjacency matrix, then ER/SR spectral measures, then binarize and assign class. A purple arrow leads to a Measure Agreement (F1 Score) bubble that compares model structures with human ones. The bottom-left green region, Microstructure Analysis, lists cultural benchmarks (CultureBench, BLEnD, CULEMO, IndoCulture, CaMel-2) feeding a Cultural Awareness block. The right blue column, Food Recommendation Study, has GPT-4o as user simulator, recommender and judge in a multi-turn conversation. It yields INT and APR scores that feed the Meta-Cultural Awareness block. Red labels mark what each part tests.

abstract: Most existing cultural evaluation frameworks for large language models (LLMs) focus on matching model outputs to ground-truth answers, primarily measuring factual cultural awareness. This overlooks whether models internalize broader cultural structure and pluralism. We introduce a spectral-analysis-based framework that captures large-scale macrostructural patterns in models' cultural knowledge and evaluate eight LLMs across nine cultural domains spanning all five of Newmark's cultural dimensions and 170 countries. Comparing with human data, we find that instruction-tuned models align more closely with human cultural structure than older models, while increased model size does not consistently improve performance. Finally, simulation-based experiments show that our proposed spectral metric better predicts a model's ability to serve users from unfamiliar cultural backgrounds than existing ones.
